title.suggested: Tom Allen starts a theater panic at the 1874 Lincoln Monument reunion

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat recalled the 1874 Army of the Tennessee reunion in Springfield, where Tom Allen crushed a pickpocket's hand in the gallery, setting off a panic that Gen. Custer calmed.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Friday Morning, May 12, 1882, page 6

facts.fact: Allen went from St. Louis to Springfield, Illinois, to attend the dedication of the National Lincoln Monument and the Army of the Tennessee reunion

At the reunion meeting in Jacob Bunn's opera house, Allen caught a pickpocket's hand and squeezed it; the man's scream began a panic in the crowded gallery, stilled when Gen. George A. Custer had the Arsenal band play
places: Jacob Bunn's opera house, Springfield, Illinois

facts.fact: Allen explained why he attended the Lincoln monument dedication
facts.quote: 'e was one of us, 'e was a man

facts.fact: Allen on the pickpocket whose hand he crushed
facts.quote: The bloody duffer, I think I broke hevry bone in 'is 'and.

notes: Retrospective written eight years after the event. The opening says Allen 'played a heroic part', but the story shows he caused the first outcry; the current summary's 'preventing disaster' is wrong. Quotes are secondhand, so medium confidence.
